name: BNY (The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation)

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Custody and clearing bank: keeps and services client assets, clears trades, moves payments, manages collateral, and runs Pershing and an asset manager. AUC/A (assets under custody and/or administration) $63.4T.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Q3 revenue $5,676M: Securities Services $2,820M (asset servicing, issuer services), Market and Wealth Services $1,984M (wealth, payments, clearance and collateral), Investment and Wealth Management $857M. Fees 72% of revenue.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Customers are banks, asset managers, corporates, issuers, broker-dealers and wealth clients; average deposits $311B. No single-customer concentration disclosed in the documents read.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: Non-US revenue 36% of total (Q3). About 25% of average deposits are non-dollar, about half of that in euros. A stronger dollar cut AUC/A and AUM growth.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Toll road: fees on assets held, trades cleared, payments moved. Fee revenue 72% of revenue; net interest income $1,423M (28%) from client deposits. Explainable in two sentences.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Q3 revenue +12%, expense +8%, operating leverage 389bp year on year; pre-tax margin 38.5% (up 2.1 points yoy but down from 39.8% in Q2). Over 3/4 of expense growth is revenue-related. Guidance hit rate: nothing_found.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical input is client cash and collateral (tags: fed_funds, 2y, real_spending, dollar). Average deposits $311B, -1% QoQ, noninterest-bearing $53B (-3% QoQ); NIM 1.43% (-2bp QoQ) with deposit margin compression. Pass-through is partial: NII +15% yoy as securities reinvest higher, but lower deposits cut it 2% QoQ. 36% non-US revenue means dollar moves change fee translation. Tech and market-utility vendors not itemised in the documents read.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Scale and switching costs: $63.4T AUC/A, 1,670 depositary receipt programs, $15.4T debt serviced, 8.8M active clearing accounts. Doing differently: platform operating model, Wealth Solutions net new assets $48B (Q3) vs $3B a year ago.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Business-to-business; the public rarely uses it directly. It would be missed by markets, not households.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Competes with other custody banks, clearing firms and technology providers (named generically in the 10-K). Share data nothing_found; growth above peers is only indirect: Issuer Services fees +43%, Asset Servicing +12% yoy.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: Clearance and collateral fees +17% yoy (average collateral $8.3T vs $7.3T); Issuer Services (Corporate Trust) +43%; average loans +19% to $86.8B. Stablecoin or tokenisation revenue: nothing_found (only GENIUS Act rules the firm is assessing, and digital asset custody listed as a service).

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: ROTCE 29.0% Q3 (29.9% YTD) vs about 10% cost of equity; 86% payout YTD; $937M buyback in Q3, new $10B authorisation (Apr 2026); diluted shares -4% yoy. Tier 1 leverage 5.7% (6.1% a year ago) and CET1 10.9% are thin. Pay: PSUs 70% adjusted ROTCE, 30% relative TSR. Insider ownership percent not found.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Embedded in market plumbing, rising relevance (Issuer Services, collateral). Risks: fee base follows market values (AUC 40% equity, 60% fixed income), deposits are rate-sensitive, key-person tie to CEO Robin Vince's retention award, AI adoption risk cited in the 10-Q.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: No 8-K Item 4.01 or 4.02, no NT filings, no material weakness found in 2022 to 2026 filing list. Non-GAAP gap small (adjusted EPS $2.37 vs $2.34). SEC comment letter on FY2022 10-K closed Oct 2023; 2024 letters are an S-3 matter (PDFs not read). Only 8-K 5.02 items are board appointments.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Boom +: fees follow asset values. Overheat +: NII +15% yoy with higher rates. Stagflation -: stocks and bonds both fall, so AUC and fees drop. Slowdown 0: falling rates cut NII, but volume, FX and collateral fees and flight-to-quality deposits help. Dollar up 4.8% trims AUC/A translation.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: Capital and liquidity rules (SLR 6.0%, LCR 111%); proposals to ease bank burdens under review. GENIUS Act: Fed proposals (Sept 24, 2026) on stablecoin reserve safekeeping and OCC final rule (Oct 21, 2026), BNY assessing. No pending deal docket.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: P/TBV 4.57x ($147.16 / $32.22 tangible book per share at Sept 30). At 10% cost of equity and 3% growth that implies a lasting ROTCE of about 35% (31% at 4% growth), vs actual 29.0% Q3, 29.9% YTD, 26% FY25. Fair P/TBV at 29.9% is 3.8x (about $124, -16%). P/E 16.3x on TTM EPS $9.05 vs own year-end P/E 12.3x (2021), 14.2x, 12.5x, 12.7x, 15.4x (2025); peers JPM 13.3x, MS 13.3x, SCHW 16.0x. Rich vs own history, no cushion.

status_reason: Strong toll-road business with delivered operating leverage, but the price implies a 35% ROTCE against 29% earned, and P/E is above its own 5-year range, so no cushion.

findings.fees_by_platform_q3: Asset Servicing $1,264M (+12% yoy), Issuer Services $449M (+43%), Wealth Solutions $554M (+7%), Payments and Trade $232M (+8%), Clearance and Collateral $464M (+17%), Investment Management $802M (+3%)
findings.margin_and_rotce: Pre-tax margin 38.5% (Q2 39.8%, Q3 2025 36.4%); ROTCE 29.0% (Q2 31.3%, 25.6% a year ago); FY25 35% margin, 26% ROTCE. Medium-term targets are referred to but their figures were not found in the documents read.
findings.auca_trend: AUC/A $63.4T, +10% yoy, +1% QoQ; AUM $2.2T, +2% yoy, -2% QoQ with Q3 net outflows $12B
findings.deposits_nii: Average deposits $311B (+4% yoy, -1% QoQ); NII $1,423M (+15% yoy, -2% QoQ); NIM 1.43%. NII guidance: nothing_found in release or presentation.
findings.operating_leverage: 389bp yoy in Q3 (revenue +12%, expense +8%); 507bp in 2025 (DEF 14A). Sequential operating leverage -184bp in Q3, and Securities Services margin fell to 35.8% from 39.3%.
findings.buybacks: Q3 $937M repurchases plus $436M dividends; YTD payout 86%; buying at about 4.5x tangible book. Shares down 3.5% yoy at 672.9M. Tier 1 leverage fell to 5.7% from 6.0% at Dec 2025.
findings.stablecoin_tokenisation: nothing_found as revenue; regulatory implementation only (GENIUS Act, Fed Sept 24 and OCC Oct 21 2026)
findings.share_price_context: Price up 33% over the year from $108.96 (Sep 30 2025) to $144.63 (Sep 30 2026); 3-year TSR +178% per DEF 14A, so the turnaround is already visible in the price
findings.routed_lead: No routed lead in routing.json named BNY

feedback.note: Q3 results support Overheat: NII +15% yoy, record fee growth with trading and FX activity; FX revenue -16% QoQ and AUC/A trimmed by the stronger dollar, consistent with the dollar read. Deposits -1% QoQ is the first sign of the funding squeeze if the Fed hikes.
